## Part 1: Theorem Questions - Answers and Tableaux

### Question 1: $\Box(A \wedge B) \rightarrow (\Box A \vee \Box B)$ in K

**Answer: YES** - This is a theorem in K. (If the conjunction is necessary, then at least one conjunct is necessary — in fact both are, so the disjunction holds trivially.)

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \wedge B) \rightarrow (\Box A \vee \Box B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box A \vee \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \wedge B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[2]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[7]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[7]}, close]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

The branch closes at world 1.1 with $\True A$ and $\False A$. (We could equally have expanded $\False \Box B$ first; that branch would close too via $\True B$ and $\False B$ at the new world.)

---

### Question 2: $(\Diamond A \vee \Diamond B) \rightarrow \Diamond(A \vee B)$ in K

**Answer: YES** - This is a theorem in K.

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, (\Diamond A \vee \Diamond B) \rightarrow \Diamond(A \vee B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond A \vee \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond(A \vee B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[4]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A \vee B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[3]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[6]}, close]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[4]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A \vee B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[3]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[6]}
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[6]}, close]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

Both branches of the disjunction close. On the left branch, $\True 1.1{:}\, A$ contradicts $\False 1.1{:}\, A$. On the right branch, $\True 1.1{:}\, B$ contradicts $\False 1.1{:}\, B$.

---

### Question 3: $\Box(A \rightarrow B) \rightarrow (\Diamond A \rightarrow \Diamond B)$ in K

**Answer: YES** - This is a theorem in K. (The "diamond version" of the K axiom.)

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \rightarrow B) \rightarrow (\Diamond A \rightarrow \Diamond B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box(A \rightarrow B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond A \rightarrow \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[5]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \rightarrow B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[2]}
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[8]}, close]
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[8]}, close]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

---

### Question 4: $\Diamond(A \wedge B) \rightarrow (\Diamond A \wedge \Diamond B)$ in K

**Answer: YES** - This is a theorem in K.

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond(A \wedge B) \rightarrow (\Diamond A \wedge \Diamond B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond A \wedge \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \wedge B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[4]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[3]}
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[7]}, close]
                        ]
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[3]}
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[9]}, close]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

---

### Question 5: $(\Diamond A \wedge \Diamond B) \rightarrow \Diamond(A \wedge B)$ in K

**Answer: NO** - This is not a theorem in K.

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, (\Diamond A \wedge \Diamond B) \rightarrow \Diamond(A \wedge B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond A \wedge \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[2]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A \wedge B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[3]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.2, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[5]}
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.2, A \wedge B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[3]}
                                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[7]}, close]
                                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[7]}
                                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.2, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[9]}]
                                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.2, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[9]}, close]
                                    ]
                                ]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

The tableau remains open on the branch where $\True 1.1{:}\, A$, $\False 1.1{:}\, B$, $\False 1.2{:}\, A$, $\True 1.2{:}\, B$. Countermodel: world 1 accesses worlds 1.1 and 1.2. At 1.1 $A$ is true and $B$ is false; at 1.2 $A$ is false and $B$ is true. So $\Diamond A$ and $\Diamond B$ both hold at world 1, but $\Diamond(A \wedge B)$ does not, since $A \wedge B$ is true at neither accessible world.

---

### Question 6: $\Box(\neg A \vee B) \rightarrow (\Box\neg A \vee \Box B)$ in K

**Answer: NO** - This is not a theorem in K.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(\neg A \vee B) \rightarrow (\Box\neg A \vee \Box B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box(\neg A \vee B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box\neg A \vee \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box\neg A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, \neg A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\neg}[6]}
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.2, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[5]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, \neg A \vee B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[2]}
                                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.2, \neg A \vee B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[2]}
                                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, \neg A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[9]}
                                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\neg}[12]}, close]
                                        ]
                                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[9]}
                                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.2, \neg A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[10]}
                                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.2, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\neg}[14]}]
                                            ]
                                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.2, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[10]}, close]
                                        ]
                                    ]
                                ]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

The tableau remains open on the branch where world 1.1 has $A$ true and $B$ true, and world 1.2 has $A$ false and $B$ false. Countermodel: world 1 accesses worlds 1.1 and 1.2. At 1.1, $A$ is true and $B$ is true (so $\neg A \vee B$ holds via $B$). At 1.2, $A$ is false and $B$ is false (so $\neg A \vee B$ holds via $\neg A$). Thus $\Box(\neg A \vee B)$ holds at world 1, but neither $\Box\neg A$ (fails at 1.1) nor $\Box B$ (fails at 1.2) holds, so the consequent is false.

---

### Question 7: $\Box(A \vee B) \rightarrow (\Diamond A \vee \Box B)$ in K

**Answer: YES** - This is a theorem in K. Intuitively: if every accessible world makes at least one of $A$ or $B$ true, then either some accessible world makes $A$ true (giving $\Diamond A$), or they all make $B$ true (giving $\Box B$).

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \vee B) \rightarrow (\Diamond A \vee \Box B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box(A \vee B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond A \vee \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[5]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[4]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \vee B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[2]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[8]}, close]
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[8]}, close]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

---

### Question 8: $\Diamond(A \rightarrow B) \rightarrow (\Box A \rightarrow \Diamond B)$ in K

**Answer: YES** - This is a theorem in K.

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond(A \rightarrow B) \rightarrow (\Box A \rightarrow \Diamond B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond(A \rightarrow B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box A \rightarrow \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \rightarrow B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[2]}
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[4]}
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[5]}
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[6]}, close]
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[6]}, close]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

---

### Question 9: $(\Box A \wedge \Diamond \neg B) \rightarrow \Diamond(A \wedge \neg B)$ in K

**Answer: YES** - This is a theorem in K.

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, (\Box A \wedge \Diamond \neg B) \rightarrow \Diamond(A \wedge \neg B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A \wedge \Diamond \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond(A \wedge \neg B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[2]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[5]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A \wedge \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[3]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[4]}
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[7]}, close]
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[7]}
                                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\neg}[10]}
                                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\neg}[6]}, close]
                                    ]
                                ]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

---

### Question 10: $\Box(A \rightarrow B) \rightarrow (\Diamond(A \wedge C) \rightarrow \Diamond(B \wedge C))$ in K

**Answer: YES** - This is a theorem in K.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \rightarrow B) \rightarrow (\Diamond(A \wedge C) \rightarrow \Diamond(B \wedge C))}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box(A \rightarrow B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond(A \wedge C) \rightarrow \Diamond(B \wedge C)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond(A \wedge C)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond(B \wedge C)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \wedge C}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B \wedge C}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[5]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[6]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, C}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[6]}
                                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \rightarrow B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[2]}
                                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[10]}, close]
                                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[10]}
                                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[7]}, close]
                                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, C}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[7]}, close]
                                        ]
                                    ]
                                ]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

### Question 11: $\Box(A \vee B) \rightarrow (\Box A \vee \Diamond B)$ in KT

**Answer: YES** - This is a theorem in KT (but not in K).

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \vee B) \rightarrow (\Box A \vee \Diamond B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box(A \vee B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box A \vee \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1, A \vee B}, just = {\TRule{\Box}{\text{T}}[2]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[4]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[6]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \vee B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[2]}
                                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[5]}
                                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[9]}, close]
                                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[9]}, close]
                                    ]
                                ]
                            ]
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[6]}
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1, B}, just = {\TRule{\Diamond}{\text{T}}[5]}, close]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

### Question 12: $\Diamond(A \wedge \neg B) \rightarrow (\Diamond A \wedge \Diamond\neg B)$ in K4

**Answer: YES** - This is a theorem already in K (the 4 axiom is not needed).

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond(A \wedge \neg B) \rightarrow (\Diamond A \wedge \Diamond\neg B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond(A \wedge \neg B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond A \wedge \Diamond\neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \wedge \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[4]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\neg}[6]}
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[3]}
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[8]}, close]
                            ]
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond\neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[3]}
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[10]}
                                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\neg}[11]}, close]
                                ]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

### Question 13: $\Box(A \rightarrow B) \rightarrow (A \rightarrow B)$ in KT

**Answer: YES** - This is a theorem in KT but not in K. The T rule extracts $A \rightarrow B$ at the actual world from the box.

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \rightarrow B) \rightarrow (A \rightarrow B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box(A \rightarrow B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, A \rightarrow B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1, A \rightarrow B}, just = {\TRule{\Box}{\text{T}}[2]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[6]}, close]
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[6]}, close]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

---

### Question 14: $\Diamond(A \vee B) \rightarrow (A \vee \Diamond B)$ in KT

**Answer: NO** - This is not a theorem in KT.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond(A \vee B) \rightarrow (A \vee \Diamond B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond(A \vee B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, A \vee \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\False}{1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \vee B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[2]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[5]}
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1, B}, just = {\TRule{\Diamond}{\text{T}}[5]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[6]}]
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[6]}, close]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

The tableau remains open on the left branch where $\True 1.1{:}\, A$, $\False 1.1{:}\, B$, $\False 1{:}\, A$, $\False 1{:}\, B$. Countermodel: world 1 has $A$ false and $B$ false; world 1.1 has $A$ true and $B$ false. World 1 accesses 1.1 (and itself, by reflexivity). Then $\Diamond(A \vee B)$ holds at 1 (via 1.1), but $A$ is false at 1 and $\Diamond B$ is false at 1 (no accessible world makes $B$ true).

### Question 15: $\Box(A \wedge B) \rightarrow \Box\Box(A \wedge B)$ in K4

**Answer: YES** - This is the 4 axiom applied to the compound sentence $A \wedge B$.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \wedge B) \rightarrow \Box\Box(A \wedge B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box\Box(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, \Box(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \wedge B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[2]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, \Box(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\Box}{\text{4}}[2]}
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[5]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[5]}
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1.1, A \wedge B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[4]}
                                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1.1, A \wedge B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[6]}
                                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[10]}
                                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[10]}
                                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[9]}, close]
                                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[9]}, close]
                                            ]
                                        ]
                                    ]
                                ]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

---

### Question 16: $\Diamond\Diamond(A \wedge \neg B) \rightarrow \Diamond(A \wedge \neg B)$ in S4

**Answer: YES** - This is an instance of the S4 principle $\Diamond\Diamond p \rightarrow \Diamond p$ with compound $p$.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond\Diamond(A \wedge \neg B) \rightarrow \Diamond(A \wedge \neg B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond\Diamond(A \wedge \neg B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond(A \wedge \neg B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, \Diamond(A \wedge \neg B)}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, \Diamond(A \wedge \neg B)}, just = {\TRule{\Diamond}{\text{4}}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1.1, A \wedge \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A \wedge \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[5]}
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.1.1, A \wedge \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[5]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[6]}
                                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1.1, \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[6]}
                                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\neg}[10]}
                                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[8]}, close]
                                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.1.1, \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[8]}
                                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\neg}[12]}, close]
                                            ]
                                        ]
                                    ]
                                ]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

## Part 2: Full Tableaux Solutions

### Problem 17: $\Box(A \vee B) \rightarrow (\neg\Box\neg A \vee \Box B)$ in K

Note: $\neg\Box\neg A$ is equivalent to $\Diamond A$, so this is really $\Box(A \vee B) \rightarrow (\Diamond A \vee \Box B)$.

We start by assuming the formula is false at world 1.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \vee B) \rightarrow (\neg\Box\neg A \vee \Box B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box(A \vee B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \neg\Box\neg A \vee \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\False}{1, \neg\Box\neg A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\vee}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box\neg A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\neg}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[5]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \vee B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[2]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, \neg A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[6]}
                                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\neg}[9]}
                                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[8]}, close]
                                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[8]}, close]
                                    ]
                                ]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

---

**Explanation:**

- Line 1: Assume the formula is false at world 1
- Lines 2-3: False conditional gives true antecedent and false consequent
- Lines 4-5: False disjunction gives both disjuncts false
- Line 6: $\False\neg\Box\neg A$ gives $\True\Box\neg A$ (false negation)
- Line 7: $\False\Box B$ introduces world 1.1 where $B$ is false
- Line 8: $\True\Box(A \vee B)$ propagates to 1.1: $\True A \vee B$
- Line 9: $\True\Box\neg A$ propagates to 1.1: $\True\neg A$
- Line 10: $\True\neg A$ gives $\False A$
- Line 11: $\True A \vee B$ branches. Left: $\True A$ contradicts $\False A$. Right: $\True B$ contradicts $\False B$.
- All branches close, so the formula is a theorem of K.

---

### Problem 18: $(\Box A \wedge \Box(A \rightarrow B)) \rightarrow \Box B$ in K

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, (\Box A \wedge \Box(A \rightarrow B)) \rightarrow \Box B}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A \wedge \Box(A \rightarrow B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box(A \rightarrow B)}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[2]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[3]}
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[4]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \rightarrow B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[5]}
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[8]}, close]
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[8]}, close]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

---

**Explanation:**

- Line 1: Assume the formula is false at world 1
- Lines 2-3: False conditional gives true antecedent and false consequent
- Lines 4-5: True conjunction gives both conjuncts true
- Line 6: $\False\Box B$ introduces world 1.1 with $\False B$
- Line 7: $\True\Box A$ propagates to 1.1: $\True A$
- Line 8: $\True\Box(A \rightarrow B)$ propagates to 1.1: $\True A \rightarrow B$
- Line 9: True conditional branches. Left: $\False A$ contradicts $\True A$ (line 7). Right: $\True B$ contradicts $\False B$ (line 6).
- All branches close, so the formula is a theorem of K.

### Problem 19: $\Box\neg(A \wedge B) \rightarrow (\Box A \rightarrow \Box\neg B)$ in K

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box\neg(A \wedge B) \rightarrow (\Box A \rightarrow \Box\neg B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box\neg(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box A \rightarrow \Box\neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box\neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[5]}
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\neg}[6]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[4]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, \neg(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[2]}
                                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A \wedge B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\neg}[9]}
                                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[10]}, close]
                                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[10]}, close]
                                    ]
                                ]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

---

**Explanation:**

- Line 1: Assume false at world 1
- Lines 2-3: False conditional
- Lines 4-5: False conditional again (nested)
- Line 6: $\False\Box\neg B$ introduces world 1.1 with $\False\neg B$
- Line 7: $\False\neg B$ gives $\True B$
- Line 8: $\True\Box A$ propagates to 1.1: $\True A$
- Line 9: $\True\Box\neg(A \wedge B)$ propagates to 1.1: $\True\neg(A \wedge B)$
- Line 10: $\True\neg(A \wedge B)$ gives $\False A \wedge B$
- Line 11: $\False A \wedge B$ branches. Left: $\False A$ contradicts $\True A$. Right: $\False B$ contradicts $\True B$.
- All branches close. This is a theorem of K.

### Problem 20: $(\Diamond\neg A \vee \Diamond\neg B) \rightarrow \Diamond\neg(A \wedge B)$ in K

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, (\Diamond\neg A \vee \Diamond\neg B) \rightarrow \Diamond\neg(A \wedge B)}, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond\neg A \vee \Diamond\neg B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Diamond\neg(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond\neg A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, \neg A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[4]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, \neg(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[3]}
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \wedge B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\neg}[6]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[7]}
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\neg}[5]}, close]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond\neg B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\vee}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, \neg B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[4]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, \neg(A \wedge B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Diamond}[3]}
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A \wedge B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\neg}[6]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[7]}
                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\neg}[5]}, close]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

---

**Explanation:**

- Line 1: Assume false at world 1
- Lines 2-3: False conditional
- Line 4: True disjunction branches
- **Left branch** ($\Diamond\neg A$): The true diamond introduces world 1.1 where $\neg A$ is true. The false diamond propagates, giving $\False\neg(A \wedge B)$ at 1.1, i.e. $\True A \wedge B$ at 1.1. Breaking up the conjunction gives $\True A$ at 1.1, but $\True\neg A$ gives $\False A$ at 1.1. Contradiction.
- **Right branch** ($\Diamond\neg B$): Similarly, we get $\True B$ from the conjunction and $\False B$ from $\neg B$. Contradiction.
- All branches close. This is a theorem of K.
